content.title: NCAA Men's Basketball Tournament Final Four Highlights: Michigan, UConn Advance
content.text: Live Coverage for this has ended Apr 04, 2026 - 11:40p ET Wolverines Are Too Tough There was no stopping Michigan in the game's final few minutes, and the Wolverines closed out the dominant win in style in front of over 72,000 fans. Michigan will now advance to its first national championship game since 2018.Apr 04, 2026 - 11:10p ET Michigan Takes 30-Point Lead Michigan guard Trey McKenny hit a 3 midway through the second half to officially make it a 30-point game, 77-47.Apr 04, 2026 - 11:00p ET Michigan Wowing Late Michigan star Aday Mara had a statement-making slam midway through the frame to further extend his team's lead.Arizona took a timeout with 12:17 to play after Wolverines guard Elliot Cadeau nailed a 3 that gave them a whopping 27-point lead, 72-45.Apr 04, 2026 - 10:54p ET Wolverines Continue To Roll The Wolverines continued to dominate as the second half got underway.Within the first few minutes, Michigan made it a 20-plus-point game.Apr 04, 2026 - 10:32p ET Michigan Cruises Into Halftime Michigan went on a run at the end of the first half and led by as many at 18 with just over a minute to play before the break. Ultimately, the Wolverines carried a 48-32 edge into halftime.Apr 04, 2026 - 10:11p ET Roddy Gayle Elevates Michigan put an end to Arizona's run midway through the opening half, and the Wolverines did it without star forward Yaxel Lendeborg, who exited the game with an injury.Senior forward Roddy Gayle brought Michigan fans to their feet after cutting to the basket and elevating for a huge two-handed flush over Arizona's 7-foot-2 center, Motiejus Krivas.Apr 04, 2026 - 10:01p ET Lendeborg Exits, Arizona Storms Back After Michigan opened up a 16-point lead in the first half, the Arizona Wildcats came storming back, putting together an 11-2 run of their own.The run began when Michigan standout Yaxel Lendeborg appeared to injure himself while driving to the basket. He was in some discomfort after getting hit on his way to the basket and went to the locker room shortly after.That's when Arizona began to storm back. After cutting the deficit to 12, Ivan Kharchenkov knocked down a deep corner 3 to make it 28-19 and bring Arizona fans to their feet.Apr 04, 2026 - 9:46p ET Michigan Jumps Out To Early Lead The Wolverines came out firing on all cylinders, jumping out to an early 10-1 lead on the Wildcats.Leading 7-1 early on, Michigan point guard Elliot Cadeau found a streaking Morez Johnson Jr., who finished a layup through contact. The Wolverines didn't slow down from there. After picking up two early fouls and heading to the bench, Michigan senior Yaxel Lendeborg came back in the game and immediately hit a corner 3, pushing the Wolverines' lead to 22-10.Apr 04, 2026 - 9:00p ET Arizona-Michigan Preview Ahead of Arizona-Michigan, one of the most famous lineups in college basketball history showed up to support their school. Michigan head football coach Kyle Whittingham was also in the house for Saturday's matchup.Apr 04, 2026 - 8:24p ET UConn Seals It UConn's Braylon Mullins came down with a huge 3 in the game's final minute to seal the Huskies' win. He and Illinois' Keaton Wagler are the first pair of opposing freshman with 15-plus points in a Final Four game since 1982.Apr 04, 2026 - 8:14p ET Solo Ball Shines UConn's Solo Ball capitalized on a turnover late in the frame, flying through the air en route to the basket to make it an eight-point game, 61-53, with just over four minutes left.Apr 04, 2026 - 8:06p ET Illini Fighting Back Late Illinois chipped away at UConn's lead late in the second half, going on a 10-0 run to cut it to a four-point game with five minutes to play.Apr 04, 2026 - 8:03p ET Huskies Cruising UConn took its biggest lead of the night — a 14-point edge — with just under 10 minutes left in the game.Apr 04, 2026 - 7:45p ET Star Power UConn, leading by double digits, continued to make one huge bucket after another in front of a star-studded crowd.Apr 04, 2026 - 7:43p ET Chaos Ensues! There was a wild string of events near the 14-minute mark when an Illinois rebound sat on the base of the rim for what felt like an eternity for Illini fans. UConn ultimately took possession after the ball finally fell.Apr 04, 2026 - 7:39p ET UConn Answers UConn answered immediately with a deep ball of its own to remain in the driver's seat as the second half continued.Apr 04, 2026 - 7:36p ET Illinois Zeroing In Illinois was pulling out all the stops early in the second half to try and cut into UConn's lead, with David Mirkovic sinking a 3 to help close the gap ever so slightly.Apr 04, 2026 - 7:34p ET Silas Demary Jr. Coming Up Clutch It was a back-and-forth battle to start the second half. UConn's Silas Demary Jr., who had been dealing with an ankle injury earlier in the tournament, knocked one in from downtown to push the Huskies' lead to double digits.Apr 04, 2026 - 7:16p ET UConn Rolling Braylon Mullins was firing on all cylinders late in the first half, as UConn continued to stretch its lead before halftime.At the break, the Huskies led by eight points, 37-29.Apr 04, 2026 - 7:14p ET Braylon Mullins Coming In Hot UConn found some momentum late in the first half after Alex Karaban ripped the ball away from Illinois, and freshman sensation Braylon Mullins came down with a monster contested bucket to keep the Huskies out front.Apr 04, 2026 - 7:06p ET Illinois Takes First Lead After trailing by as many as nine early on, Illinois caught fire midway through the first half. Tomislav Ivisic helped fuel a 13-3 run by the Fighting Illini after head coach Brad Underwood called an early timeout at the 13:20 mark. The 7-foot-1 junior knocked down a huge 3 to give Illinois its first lead of the game.Apr 04, 2026 - 7:06p ET Tarris Reed Jr. Taking Over UConn's Tarris Reed Jr. has been near unstoppable throughout this year's NCAA Tournament, and the senior big man started right where he left off for the Huskies.Holding onto an early 16-9 lead, Reed slipped to the basket, caught a pass from fellow senior Alex Karaban and threw down a thunderous two-handed slam through contact, capping a 10-2 run for UConn.Apr 04, 2026 - 5:09p ET UConn-Illinois Preview UConn is one game away from making its third title game in four years, should the Huskies get past Illinois, which is back in the Final Four for the first time since 2005. Keep an eye on standouts Silas Demary Jr. and Tarris Reed Jr., whose presence could foreshadow what's next for the Huskies; The last time UConn won a national championship the team also had two players who had transferred in from the power conferences.
